name: tsid
description:
Generate a new Time-Sorted Unique Identifier as a 32-character lowercase hex string. The first 64 bits hold the generation time (seconds and nanoseconds since the Unix epoch), so ordinary string comparison sorts by generation time; the remaining 62 bits are random and the layout carries UUID version 4 and variant bits. Concurrent calls and clock changes do not establish strict insertion order.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** `tsid(ts)` takes a `TIMESTAMP` (1970-01-01 to 2106-02-07) and embeds that time instead of the current one — useful for backfilling or for building ID range bounds; out-of-range or infinite timestamps raise an error and `NULL` returns `NULL`. The random tail comes from a per-thread generator seeded from the operating system (`std::random_device`) instead of one clock-seeded generator shared by all threads.

examples.code: SELECT tsid() AS id FROM range(100);

examples.description: DuckDB 2.0 build: an ID for a given time — the embedded timestamp round-trips

name: tsid_uuid
description: **DuckDB 2.0 build only.** Generate a TSID as a native `UUID` value: the same bits, layout and time ordering as `tsid()`, stored in 16 bytes instead of a 32-character string. `UUID` comparison follows the byte order, so `ORDER BY` sorts by generation time. `tsid_uuid(ts)` embeds a given `TIMESTAMP` (1970-01-01 to 2106-02-07). Decode with `tsid_to_timestamp`. The value is version-4-shaped, so DuckDB's `uuid_extract_timestamp` (which reads UUIDv7) does not apply.

name: tsid_to_timestamp
description:
Extract the embedded timestamp from a TSID. Returns `TIMESTAMP` (microsecond precision) — the time the ID was generated, or the time passed to `tsid(ts)`. Accepts the 32-hex-digit form or the dashed 8-4-4-4-12 form, in either case. NULL input returns NULL; any other string raises a Conversion Error (`Invalid TSID format`) — wrap it in `TRY()` to get NULL instead.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** also accepts a native `UUID` (from `tsid_uuid()` or a cast). Parsing is strict: a 36-character string must have its dashes at the 8-4-4-4-12 positions. Earlier builds could crash the process on some malformed 36-character strings and decoded an all-dash string as 1970-01-01.

examples.description: Recover when a row was inserted from its id alone
examples.code: SELECT id, tsid_to_timestamp(id) AS created_at FROM events;
